nodes.relay.title: Connection mode
nodes.relay.modeHelp: Adds a client traffic entry only; Node control address, control/API ports and certificates are unchanged.
nodes.relay.addressHelp: Use the main server's direct IP or DNS-only hostname, not a CDN-proxied address.
nodes.relay.portHelp: Checked on save. Auto starts at 18443 and retains existing ports.
nodes.relay.invalidPort: Enter a valid port from 1024 to 65535.
nodes.relay.targetHelp: First release: VLESS TCP/RAW REALITY only. Not a Node control/API port.
nodes.relay.noInbound: No compatible VLESS TCP REALITY inbound exists in the core configuration.
nodes.relay.exitHelp: The main server is only the entry; this Node and its residential egress determine the exit.
nodes.relay.directHelp: Uses existing direct entries; host settings are unchanged.
nodes.relay.preserved: Main-server exit and all original direct entries are preserved. A listening entry is not proof of public connectivity.
nodes.relay.applyHelp: Saved independently. Applying can briefly interrupt relay sessions, not main/Node cores. Allow the entry TCP port in the firewall/security group.

hostsDialog.port.info: By default, a host uses the default port of the inbound. You can set a custom port in case this host is a server that forwards traffic from a port that differs from your server's port. For example, the server may forward traffic from port 8443 to the default port of your inbound server.
hostsDialog.proxyOutbound.info: Extra outbound ( only in v2ray custom config )
hostsDialog.security.info: If the middleware server of this host uses a different security layer than the inbound's default, you can set a custom security layer here.
hostsDialog.sni.info: By default, a host uses the default SNI of the inbound. You can set a custom SNI in case this host is a server that has a different SNI. For example, the server may receive traffic with a different SSL certificate, perform SSL termination, and forward it to your inbound server.

nodes.egress.title: Residential IP / outbound proxy
nodes.egress.hint: Each Marzban-Node has one independent outbound. Choose its UDP handling below; deploy the paired Marzban-Node first.
nodes.egress.udpHelp: TCP-only mode tunnels fallback UDP port 53 DNS over residential TCP and blocks other fallback UDP. It replaces this Node's dns.servers with TCP DNS 1.1.1.1 / 8.8.8.8. Existing explicit routes retain priority; no direct fallback is added. Games and voice apps still require provider UDP support; arbitrary UDP is not converted to TCP.

nodes.egress.cleared: Node outbound removed; restoring direct route
